fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure; Perimeter Fencing; Dense Vegetation; Open Green Space
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responding units identify the property quickly from the road.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the driveway to maintain a clear path wide enough for emergency vehicles to reach the front of the residence.
• Cut back any dense shrubs or tree branches overhanging the driveway to allow ladder trucks and taller emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Clear a staging area near the front parking area and keep it free of parked vehicles to give arriving units an unobstructed working space.
• Thin dense vegetation growing close to the detached structure to allow responders to move around all sides of it without obstruction.
• Create a clear foot path along the perimeter fencing that allows responders to move from the front of the property to the rear without pushing through dense vegetation.
• Mark or clearly identify any gate in the perimeter fencing that provides the most direct route to the rear of the property.
• Keep any rear gate unlocked or secured with a combination lock with the code shared with the local fire department.
• Remove or thin dense vegetation growing directly against or immediately around any structure to allow responders to work close to exterior walls.
• Post the property address visibly at both the street and the driveway entrance if the main entrance is not directly visible from the road.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Mixed Vegetation; Brush Area; Tall Grass Area; Ground Vegetation; Scattered Shrubs; Single Access Route; Limited Rear Access; Open Green Space
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the cluster closest to the structure to create more open space between individual trees and the building.
• Remove or cut back shrubs and brush that are growing directly against or touching the structure.
• Cut tall grass areas near the structure down to a low height before dry season.
• Clear ground vegetation growing up against the base of the structure on all accessible sides.
• Thin scattered shrubs near the structure so individual plants are separated and not touching each other.
• Remove dead material from within the brush area closest to the structure.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation at all times.
• Trim any tree branches that hang over or touch the driveway to maintain full vehicle clearance.
• Clear brush and tall grass along the edges of the driveway so it remains passable from both directions.
• Cut back vegetation along whatever rear access exists to keep that path open for foot or equipment movement.
• Maintain the open green space by keeping grass cut short and removing any woody plants or brush that begin to establish there.
• Separate any scattered trees near the structure so their branches do not touch each other or the building.
• Remove accumulated dead leaves, grass, and plant debris from the ground around the base of the structure.
